description: A WordPress site imported into this Frappe site: its pages become Web Pages, posts Blog Posts, media Files and Gravity Forms entries CRM Leads. Re-running an import updates what changed and skips what didn't.

fields.description: Imported by the hourly schedule. A disabled source can still be imported by hand.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: The WordPress site's address, e.g. https://example.com.
fields.label: Site URL

fields.description: The WordPress user the Application Password belongs to. Needs to read drafts, media and Gravity Forms entries (an administrator, or a role with those capabilities).
fields.label: WordPress Username

fields.description: A WordPress Application Password (Users → Profile). Used for both the WordPress and Gravity Forms REST APIs.
fields.label: Application Password

fields.description: Route segment imported pages live under (e.g. a Public Site's route prefix): page "about" becomes the Web Page routed <prefix>/about; the front page becomes <prefix>/home.
fields.label: Route Prefix

fields.description: WordPress page id of the front page. Empty: read from the site's reading settings.
fields.label: Front Page ID

fields.description: Blog Category (blog app) imported posts are filed under.
fields.label: Blog Category

fields.description: Blogger (blog app) imported posts are attributed to.
fields.label: Blogger

fields.description: CRM Lead Source given to leads imported from form entries (optional).
fields.label: Lead Source

fields.description: Media library items become public Files; pages and posts link to them instead of WordPress.
fields.label: Media

fields.description: Active Gravity Forms entries become CRM Leads (Frappe CRM). Spam and trashed entries are skipped.
fields.label: Form Entries

fields.description: Each form's fields map to lead fields automatically (name, email, phone, website, company). A row here overrides one input; anything unmapped is kept in the lead's form message.
fields.label: Form Field Maps

name: WordPress Source
